verified_structurally.authority_frame_source: commissionAuthorityFrame() is built ONLY from dispatcher-held values (commission_path, commission_sha256, terrain, role, worktree, holds); it never reads the commission
verified_structurally.byte_integrity: sha256 of exact delivered bytes checked before launch; drift raises COMMISSION_DELIVERY_DRIFT
verified_structurally.defang_is_load_bearing: the RENDERED (defanged) document is what --file attaches; the untouched bytes remain the integrity anchor

defang_attack_reviewer_authored.legitimate_content: ordinary prose, code spans, '==' assertions and terrain lines pass untouched; a bare fence is defanged by design

MR5_commission_delivery_integrity.bounded_property_actually_established: The defang is a LINE-ANCHORED PRESENTATION GUARD: it reliably prevents the attachment from LOOKING like a tool call at line start. It is NOT an injection filter and does not sanitise arbitrary instruction-looking content.
MR5_commission_delivery_integrity.why_not_a_soundness_break: the security property does not rest on defang; it rests on the dispatcher-generated precedence frame plus byte integrity. Defang is defence-in-depth for one presentation family.
MR5_commission_delivery_integrity.NOT_claimed: no prompt-injection immunity. Residual risk is the model's own instruction-following, which no dispatcher-side transform removes.
MR5_commission_delivery_integrity.not_verified_live: the 'legitimate task still completes' half (CLI could not run under the review sandbox)

MR6_lock_and_durability.reviewer_test_correction: my first attempt wrote the lock as JSON; the parser expects 'pid=N token=HEX', so my initial FAIL was a harness bug, not a candidate defect. Corrected and re-run.

results.scenario: LIVE owner (own pid) with mtime 900s old

MR6_lock_and_durability.mtime_robbery_fixed: ownership is now decided by process.kill(pid,0) with EPERM counted alive; the old mtime>30s reclaim is gone
MR6_lock_and_durability.token_guarded_release: release removes the lock only when the token still matches, so a predecessor cannot evict a successor's lock
MR6_lock_and_durability.directory_fsync: state directory IS fsynced on log creation (openSync(dir,'r') + fsyncSync); my earlier flag was a false positive corrected on inspection
